Hon'ble Rajeev Singh,J.
1.
Heard Sri Shyam Manohar, learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A for the State of U.P.
and perused the record.

2. The present bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in Case Crime No.803 of 2017, under Sections 376, 323, 506 I.P.C., Police Station- Maurawan, District- Unnao with the prayer to enlarge him on bail.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is an innocent person and has been falsely implicated in the present case and he is in jail since 28.05.2018.

He further submits that Suraj Yadav @ Surya Prakash vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139892737/

sentences.text: criminal antecedent of 08 cases against applicant was shown but in 03 cases he was not named.

He further submits that investigation was conducted by Investigating Officer in most mechanical manner and charge-sheet was submitted merely on the basis of statement of victim recorded U/s 161 as well as 164 Cr.P.C.
During the course of trial, statement of victim was recorded and there was a contradiction in her statement.

He further submits that earlier bail application was rejected by this Court on 21.02.2022 in Bail Application No.323 of 2019, thereafter, against the aforesaid bail rejection order an S.L.P. was preferred before Hon'ble Apex Court which was disposed of on 06.12.2022 with the observation that applicant may apply fresh application for bail.

At the time of deciding the first bail application on 21.02.2022, direction was issued to trial court to conclude the trial within one year from the date of passing the order but till today trial has not been concluded.

He draws attention of the Court on the judgement of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Prabhakar Tewari vs. State of U.P. and another reported in (2020) 11 SCC 648 and submits that pendency of several criminal cases will not be a ground for refusal of bail.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is, thus, submitted that there is no possibility of conclusion of trial in near future, in these circumstances, the applicant is entitled for bail.
In case of being enlarged on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
4. Learned A.G.A. opposes the prayer for grant of bail to the applicant and submits that five witnesses have already been examined out of eight witness.

He does not dispute this fact that applicant is in jail since28.05.2018 and direction was given to trial court by this Court on 21.02.2022 that the trial of case be concluded within one year but trial has not been concluded till today.

5. Considering the rival submissions of learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. and going through the contents of bail application as well as first bail rejection order dated 21.02.2022, in which, direction was given to trial court to conclude the trial within one year, thereafter, S.L.P. dated 06.12.2022 was also preferred which was disposed of by Hon'ble Apex Court with the observation that applicant may file fresh application for bail.

In case of long trial, the pendency of criminal cases against the applicant will not be a ground for refusal of bail; as applicant is in jail since28.05.2018 but till today trial has not been concluded.
I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.

6. Let the applicant, namely,Suraj Yadav @ Surya Prakash who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
(i) The applicant shall not commit or participate in any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.

sentences.text: In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.

(iv) The applicant shall remain present before the Trial Court on each date fixed,
either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the Trial Court may proceed against him under Section 229-A IPC.

(v) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C., may be issued and if applicant fails to appear before the Court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the Trial Court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under Section 174-A IPC.
(vi) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
7. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
